question: What is the main job of the pulmonary circulation system?

options.A: To supply oxygen to body tissues
options.B: To filter waste from the kidneys
options.D: To oxygenate blood in the lungs

explanation: You've got this! The pulmonary circuit's special mission is to send blood through the lungs so it can pick up fresh oxygen and drop off carbon dioxide. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h1)

question: How is pulmonary circulation different from systemic circulation?

options.A: It operates under much higher pressure limits
options.B: It pumps blood only to and from the lungs
options.C: It uses arteries to carry only oxygenated blood
options.D: It bypasses the heart chambers completely

explanation: Great thinking! While systemic circulation serves the whole body, pulmonary circulation is just a short, dedicated loop between the heart and the lungs. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h1)

question: Which heart chamber pumps deoxygenated blood into the pulmonary trunk?
explanation: Spot on! The right ventricle is the muscular pump that pushes deoxygenated blood out toward the lungs. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h2)

question: How many pulmonary veins normally bring oxygen-rich blood back to the left atrium?
explanation: You're doing great! Typically, you have two left and two right pulmonary veins safely carrying that fresh, oxygenated blood back to the heart. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h2)

question: Which blood vessel takes deoxygenated blood straight out of the right ventricle?
explanation: Awesome! The pulmonary trunk catches the blood right as it leaves the right ventricle before branching off into the lungs. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h3)

question: What is the correct path of blood as it travels from the heart to the lungs?

options.A: Capillaries to arteries to trunk to ventricle
options.B: Atrium to veins to capillaries to arteries
options.C: Ventricle to trunk to arteries to capillaries
options.D: Trunk to ventricle to capillaries to veins

explanation: Keep it up! Blood flows smoothly from the pumping chamber (ventricle) into the main trunk, out through branching arteries, and finally into the tiny alveolar capillaries. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h3)

question: How does oxygen cross the tiny air sacs in the lungs to enter the blood?
explanation: You're learning fast! Oxygen molecules simply glide across the super-thin respiratory membrane from a high area to a low area without needing any energy. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h4)

question: In which direction does carbon dioxide travel during gas exchange in the lungs?

options.A: From the pulmonary veins to tissue cells
options.B: From the left atrium to the lungs
options.C: From the alveoli into the blood
options.D: From the blood into the alveoli

explanation: Spot on! Carbon dioxide is waste, so it moves out of the blood and into the alveoli (air sacs) so you can breathe it out. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h4)

question: Why is blood pressure in the lungs much lower than in the rest of the body?

options.A: The lungs offer very low vascular resistance
options.C: The left ventricle pumps with less force
options.D: Blood volume in the lungs is extremely small

explanation: Brilliant! Because the path is short and the blood vessels in the lungs are wide and stretchy, the blood flows easily without building up high pressure. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h5)

question: What do the small lung blood vessels do when a specific part of the lung isn't getting enough oxygen?

options.A: They dilate to force more blood through
options.B: They rupture due to sudden pressure buildup
options.C: They constrict to redirect blood elsewhere
options.D: They permanently close and form scar tissue

explanation: Clever body design! These vessels narrow down (constrict) to push blood away from lazy, unventilated air sacs and send it toward areas that are breathing better. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h5)

question: What is a pulmonary embolism?

options.A: A blood clot blocking a pulmonary arterial branch
options.B: Fluid accumulation inside the left heart chambers
options.C: An infection of the alveolar-capillary membrane
options.D: The dilation of major veins entering the atrium

explanation: You've got this! A pulmonary embolism happens when a traveling blood clot (often starting in the legs) gets stuck in one of the lung's blood vessels. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h6)

question: What heart condition is caused by long-term high blood pressure in the lungs straining the right side of the heart?
explanation: Ending strong! Cor pulmonale happens when the right ventricle has to work way too hard against high lung pressure, leading to right-sided heart strain. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h6)
